newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British ex-minister Howe to attend HK swearing in.
newsitem.headline: British ex-minister Howe to attend HK swearing in.

text.p: Former British foreign secretary Lord Geoffrey Howe will attend the swearing in of a controversial unelected legislature in Hong Kong after the territory's handover to China, Hong Kong government radio said on Monday.
Lord Howe, who in 1984 negotiated the return of Hong Kong to China that will formally take place at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday, had said he would be present, the radio said.
The Provisional Legislature, appointed by China, will replace a democratically elected chamber and will be sworn in shortly after Hong Kong's handover to Beijing at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
British Prime Minister Tony Blair and Foreign Secretary Robin Cook, along with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, plan to boycott the ceremony, although both countries are sending diplomats.
Howe was quoted as saying disagreements about the elected Legislative Council being abolished by Beijing were a thing of the past.
